info.title: Arker Public VM API
info.description:
Public VM API contract. Backends expose the same endpoint and wire
shapes; backend-specific feature limitations are returned as
`ErrorResponse` with `code: "unsupported_operation"`.

post.description:
Create a new VM by forking from an image, an existing VM ID, or
a VM name within an org. Exactly one of `source_image`,
`source_vm_id`, or `source_vm_name` must be set. Forking a VM
owned by another org requires that VM to be `public: true`.

parameters.name: region
parameters.description: Narrow to a single backend region (e.g. `us-west-2`). When omitted, the response aggregates across every configured region.

parameters.name: provider
parameters.description: Narrow to a single backend provider. `aws` returns only arkerd-managed (host-backed) VMs; `aws-burst` returns only Lambda-managed VMs. When omitted, both are returned merged.

parameters.name: started_after
parameters.description: ISO 8601 timestamp; include only VMs that most recently started at or after this time.

parameters.name: started_before
parameters.description: ISO 8601 timestamp; include only VMs that most recently started at or before this time.

200.description: VMs visible to the authenticated caller.

post.description:
Run a command. Foreground execution is the portable baseline.
Optional `background`, `session_id`, `network`, `signal`,
`acquire`/`release`, and per-run resource overrides may return
`unsupported_operation` on backends that don't support them.

Create a persistent sync: ensure a Filesystem exists (creating
one if requested) and bind-mount it into this VM at `path`.
Bidirectional by virtue of being a mount — there is no separate
sync-direction parameter. Returns `ErrorResponse` code
`conflict` if a sync already exists at `path`.

200.description: Read or write result, matching the request op.

post.description: Read or write files in the VM filesystem (including mounted sync paths). Discriminated by `op`: `{ "op": "read", "path" }` reads a file (inline content for small files, a presigned GET URL for large ones); `{ "op": "write", "writes": [...] }` writes, where each entry is an inline chunk or a presigned-upload step. Binding a standalone filesystem into the VM is a separate operation — see `POST /v1/vms/{id}/syncs`.

200.description: Delete result. The filesystem must not be mounted by any VM (no remaining `Sync` referencing it).

Cursor.name: cursor
Cursor.description: Opaque pagination cursor returned by the previous page's `next_cursor`.

Limit.name: limit
Limit.description: Max items per page. Backend caps may apply.

UnsupportedOperation.description: The request is valid, but this backend does not support the requested operation or option.

value.message: background runs are not supported on this backend

ErrorCode.description: Stable machine-readable error code. `unsupported_operation` means the backend doesn't implement the requested optional feature.

VmState.description: Unified lifecycle state for a VM or a Session. `idle` means no command is currently executing; `running` means a command is in flight.

RunState.description:
Unified lifecycle state for a Run. `cancelled` covers both
client cancellation and server-side abort. Failure is NOT a
state — failed runs land in `completed` with non-zero
`exit_code`.

TunnelState.description:
`starting` = backend is allocating the tunnel; `open` = accepting
connections; `closed` = torn down or never came up.

source_vm_id.description: Global VM identifier. Org is inferred from the row.

source_vm_name.description: VM name within an org. Defaults `source_org_id` to the caller's org. A different org must be either the Arker org (for the public goldens `arkuntu` / `ubuntu`) or one with a `public: true` VM by that name.

source_org_id.description: Optional explicit org context for `source_vm_name`. SDK auto-fills the Arker org when forking the public goldens.

name.description: Optional name for the new VM, scoped to the caller's org.

public.description: Make the new VM publicly forkable from other orgs.

tunnels.description: Optional inbound tunnel allocation at fork time.

env.description: Optional environment-variable overrides for this session.

public.description: When `true`, other orgs can fork this VM (but cannot run on it).

root_source_vm_id.description: ID of the root (deepest-ancestor) source VM, if this VM was created by a chain of forks. None for VMs forked directly from an image.

root_source_vm_name.description: Name of the root source VM. Populated together with `root_source_vm_id`.

worker_id.description: Worker host that owns this VM. Used by routers to populate caches without a fresh PlanetScale lookup.

acquire.description:
Comma-separated list of resources to ensure are
pre-allocated (warm) before the run starts. Values: `cpu`,
`memory`, `disk`. Example: `"cpu,memory"`.

release.description:
Comma-separated list of resources to release after the run
finishes. Values: `cpu`, `memory`, `disk`. `"cpu"` frees
vCPU but keeps memory hot for the next run on this VM;
`"cpu,memory,disk"` is a full release (closest to a
suspend).

stdout_encoding.description:
TODO(encoding-normalize): goal is to always emit utf-8 from
every source so this field becomes unnecessary. Until then
the SDK uses it to decode.

vm_id.description: The VM this tunnel belongs to. Always populated, including when embedded in `Run.tunnels`.

run_id.description: The Run that opened this tunnel, if any. Tunnels allocated at fork time have `run_id: null`.

path.description: VM-side path where the filesystem is mounted. Same field name as used by `SyncReadRequest.path`.
VM-side path. Returns `ErrorResponse` code `conflict` if a sync already exists at this path.
